walkthroughs.body_html:
Some poems explore how humans wield power — and lose it.

Ozymandias (Shelley), London (Blake), My Last Duchess (Browning) and Tissue (Dharker) all show authority crumbling or controlling people unjustly.

Other poems pit man against nature.

The Prelude (Wordsworth), Storm on the Island (Heaney) and Exposure (Owen) show nature humbling, frightening or killing the human speaker.

The third strand is war and its memory.

Charge of the Light Brigade (Tennyson), Bayonet Charge (Hughes), Remains (Armitage), War Photographer (Duffy), Poppies (Weir), Kamikaze (Garland), The Émigrée (Rumens) and Checking Out Me History (Agard) all explore conflict's human cost.
